properties.name: `claude mcp get` takes a NAME and no `--scope` (only `add` and `remove` do), so the registration check passed an unknown option, fell through its exception path and answered "not registered" regardless of truth. Found by running --check on a machine that had genuinely never been installed: the answer looked right for the wrong reason. The check now asks the question the CLI can actually answer — is a server of this name visible at ANY scope — and says so in its own output rather than guessing "create" vs "update". Behaviour of the install itself is unchanged: registration was always unconditional, because it is idempotent.
